HEALTH_DECLINED: No problem, I'll just ask you.

onboarding.MEMORY_ASK: Can I remember the little things you tell me, like your walks? It helps me make better suggestions. You can change this any time.
onboarding.MEMORY_NO: That's fine, just your answers then.
onboarding.MEMORY_WHY: If you tell me you walk your dog in the mornings, I can suggest something that fits your day. It stays on your phone, and you can change your mind any time.
onboarding.SUPPLEMENT_REPLY: That's a good one to ask your pharmacist or doctor. Bring your bottles to your next visit so they can check them with your other medicines.
UNKNOWN_ACKS: That's okay, we'll leave it out.
No problem, I'll leave that blank.
onboarding.UNKNOWN_FIRST: Your twin will say it's still learning.
onboarding.HOW_ARE_YOU: I'm doing well, thank you for asking!
onboarding.ESTIMATE_NOTE: That's a rough estimate from what you said.
onboarding.BP_READING: Thanks, {reading}. A single reading isn't the same as a diagnosis, so I'll just ask:

age.label: age
ask: How old are you?
To start, how old are you?
age.help: I'm asking how many years old you are today. For example, say "I'm 72". You can also tell me the year you were born.

sex.label: sex
ask: What sex were you at birth: female or male?
Were you born female or male?
sex.help: I'm asking whether you were born female or male, because health numbers differ between the two. Just say "female" or "male".

smoking_status.label: smoking
ask: Do you smoke now, did you smoke before, or have you never smoked?
Do you smoke now, did you use to, or have you never smoked?
smoking_status.help: I'm asking about smoking cigarettes. Say "never" if you never smoked, "I quit" if you smoked in the past, or "I smoke" if you smoke now.

height_cm.label: height
ask: How tall are you? For example, 5 feet 10 inches.
height_cm.help: I'm asking how tall you are, standing without shoes. For example, "5 feet 10 inches" or "178 cm". A close guess is fine.

weight_kg.label: weight
ask: How much do you weigh? For example, 160 pounds.
And about how much do you weigh? For example, 160 pounds.
weight_kg.help: I'm asking how much you weigh. For example, "160 pounds" or "72 kg". A close guess is fine. I'll read it back to you.

sleep_hours.label: sleep
ask: How many hours do you sleep on a usual night?
On a usual night, about how many hours do you sleep?
sleep_hours.help: I'm asking how many hours you sleep on a usual night. For example, "7 hours", or "from 11 at night to 6 in the morning".
sleep_hours.proxy: That's okay. What time do you usually go to bed, and when do you get up?

general_health.label: health
ask: How would you rate your health: excellent, very good, good, fair or poor?
Overall, is your health excellent, very good, good, fair or poor?
general_health.help: I'm asking how you'd rate your own health in general. There's no right answer. Just pick one: excellent, very good, good, fair or poor.
general_health.proxy: That's fine. On most days, do you feel great, pretty good, okay, not so good, or poorly?

hypertension_diagnosed.label: high blood pressure
ask: Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure?
Has a doctor ever said you have high blood pressure?
hypertension_diagnosed.help: I'm asking whether a doctor has ever told you that you have high blood pressure, also called hypertension. A single reading doesn't count. Say yes, no, or "not sure".

diabetes.label: diabetes
ask: Has a doctor ever told you that you have diabetes?
And has a doctor ever told you that you have diabetes?
diabetes.help: I'm asking if a doctor has ever told you that you have diabetes, also called high blood sugar. Say "yes", "no", or "I'm not sure".

sedentary_min_day.label: sitting time
ask: About how many hours a day do you spend sitting? TV and driving count.
On a usual day, how many hours do you sit? TV and driving count.
sedentary_min_day.help: I'm asking how long you sit on a usual day while you're awake: at the table, in a chair, in the car. A rough guess is fine, like "6 hours".
sedentary_min_day.proxy: That's okay. Do you sit most of the day, about half, or are you on your feet most of the day?
proxy_replies: On my feet most of the day

moderate_recreation_min_week.label: lighter activity
ask: In a usual week, how many minutes of lighter activity do you do, like brisk walking or gardening?
How many minutes a week of lighter activity, like brisk walking or gardening?
moderate_recreation_min_week.help: I'm asking about activity that gets you a little out of breath, like a brisk walk, gardening or dancing. Add up a usual week. A 30-minute walk, 5 days a week, is 150 minutes. If you don't do any, say "none".
moderate_recreation_min_week.proxy: That's okay. Do you walk, garden or dance at all?

vigorous_recreation_min_week.label: harder exercise
ask: And harder exercise that makes you breathe hard, like jogging or tennis? How many minutes a week?
Any harder exercise, like jogging or tennis? How many minutes a week?
vigorous_recreation_min_week.help: I'm asking about exercise that makes you breathe hard and talk only in short bursts, like jogging, fast cycling or singles tennis. "None" is a fine answer.
vigorous_recreation_min_week.proxy: That's okay. Do you ever do anything that leaves you out of breath?
vigorous_recreation_min_week.with_health: Apple Health shows about {total} of activity a week. How much of it makes you breathe hard, like jogging?

exercise_minutes_weekly.label: exercise
ask: About how many minutes do you exercise in a week? A 30-minute walk, 5 days a week, is 150 minutes.
exercise_minutes_weekly.help: I'm asking how many minutes you move on purpose in a whole week, like walking, swimming or gardening. For example, a 30-minute walk 5 days a week is "150 minutes". If you don't exercise, say "none".

alcohol_drinks_weekly.label: alcohol
ask: How many alcoholic drinks do you have in a week? Say none if you don't drink.
alcohol_drinks_weekly.help: I'm asking how many drinks of beer, wine or liquor you have in a usual week. One beer or one glass of wine is one drink. For example, "3 drinks", or "none".

systolic_bp.label: top blood pressure number
ask: What is your blood pressure? For example, 120 over 80.
systolic_bp.help: I'm asking for your blood pressure: the two numbers a blood pressure cuff shows, the bigger one first. For example, "120 over 80". If you don't know it, say "I don't know".

diastolic_bp.label: bottom blood pressure number
ask: What is the bottom number of your blood pressure? For example, the 80 in 120 over 80.
diastolic_bp.help: I'm asking for the bottom, smaller number of your blood pressure. For example, the 80 in "120 over 80". If you don't know it, say "I don't know".

change.GREETING: Hi, it's Mochi! What would you like to update?
change.CHOOSE_AGAIN: Sorry, I didn't catch that. You can update your weight, height, sleep, exercise, drinks, smoking, blood pressure, diabetes or age. What would you like to update?
change.ONE_AT_A_TIME: Let's do one at a time. Which would you like to update first: {}?
change.ALSO: You also mentioned your {}. Would you like to update that too?
change.RESTART: Okay, let's start again. Nothing has changed. What would you like to update?
change.DELETE_NOTE: To remove all your answers, use "Delete my data" in Settings.
change.PROBE: Thank you. Before I read it back: did something change, like a new routine?
change.SAME: That's the same as what I have, so nothing needs to change.
change.KEPT: Okay, I'll leave it as it is. Nothing has changed.
change.DONE_AGAIN: We're all done. If something else changes, just tap Update.
change.CANCELLED: Okay, we'll leave it there. Nothing has changed.
change.OTHERS: I can only change your own answers, not anyone else's.
change.SEX_FIXED: Sex at birth can't be changed here. Your twin's forecast is built on it, so it stays as you first told me. If it was saved by mistake, "Delete my data" in Settings lets you start fresh.
change.ANYTHING_ELSE: Is there anything else you'd like to update?
change.AGE_RULE: Your age only changes on your birthday, so I can't change it from {old} to {new}. If you've had a birthday, just tell me, and I'll make it {next}.
change.DOCTOR_QUESTION: Did a doctor tell you that you have diabetes?
change.DIABETES_NO_DOCTOR: Okay. I only add diabetes when a doctor has told you, so I'll leave it as it is. If you're worried, your doctor can check. Nothing has changed.
change.DIABETES_STAYS: This answer is about whether a doctor has ever told you that you have diabetes, so it stays the same even when it's well managed. Nothing has changed.
change.BP_NO_READING: That's okay. When you have a new reading, we can update it. Nothing has changed.
change.BP_TALK: Thanks for telling me. I keep your blood pressure as its two numbers.
change.BOTH_BP: Please tell me both blood pressure numbers, for example "135 over 85".
change.WHY_NOTE: I check every change with you, so your twin uses what's true for you now. Your answers stay on your phone, and LifeTwin's server doesn't keep them. Nothing changes until you say yes.
change.PRIVATE_NOTE: Your answers stay on your phone. LifeTwin's server uses them for your forecast but doesn't keep them. Nothing changes until you say yes.
change.MEMORY_NOTE: I'll only remember why it changed because you said that's okay.
change.HELP_CHOOSING: Tell me what's different, like "I lost some weight" or "I quit smoking". I'll read it back to you before anything changes.
change.HELP_PROBING: I'd like to know what's behind the change, like a new routine or a doctor's advice. If you'd rather not say, just say "skip".
change.HELP_CONFIRMING: I'm checking that I heard you right before I change anything. {} If that's right, say "yes". If not, say "no" and then the right answer.
change.NEVER_MIND: If nothing has changed, just say "never mind".
